headline: Highest risk is data leakage: dbt-core can reach a data warehouse while Botpress may ingest and relay content, but the pairwise interaction is only docs-level and unverified.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented shared channel to dbt-core, and dbt-core is a data-engineering tool that calls data-warehouse APIs. A prompt-injection path is not evidenced by the profiles; the only plausible bridge would be manual copy/paste or an external workspace not shown here, so severity stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF Botpress output is manually pasted into dbt-core prompts or docs, injection becomes plausible.
IF an external shared workspace is added between the agents, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy/paste handoff of untrusted text.
Add a human review step before reusing Botpress-generated content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can call warehouse APIs, while Botpress is a support agent that may surface user content. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem or explicit secret handling, so leakage is inferred rather than direct; still, default warehouse access plus support content creates a plausible sensitive-data flow in normal use.
conditions: IF Botpress is given customer tickets containing sensitive data and that content is forwarded into dbt-core workflows, leakage risk increases.
IF dbt-core queries production warehouse tables containing regulated data, outputs may expose sensitive fields.
mitigations: Restrict dbt-core to masked or nonproduction schemas.
Redact support-ticket content before any handoff.
Use separate credentials for support and analytics workflows.
Review warehouse query logs for sensitive columns.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress has install_packages but no write or network egress beyond none, while dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and warehouse API access. The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces, shared mutable state, or locking issues, so direct capability conflict is limited and likely requires unusual orchestration not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable warehouse objects, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator grants Botpress write access not shown in the profile, contention risk rises.
mitigations: Assign separate resource scopes.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same warehouse objects.
Schedule dbt runs outside Botpress maintenance windows.
Confirm Botpress has no hidden write path.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support-facing content, and dbt-core can act on warehouse data transformations. The profiles do not prove that dbt-core consumes Botpress output directly, but if it does, B may treat A's generated text as authoritative without verification. That makes cascading error plausible in default integration patterns, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF dbt-core ingests Botpress-generated instructions or SQL without validation, errors can cascade.
IF Botpress is used to draft transformation logic that dbt-core executes, downstream mistakes propagate.
mitigations: Require human approval for generated SQL.
Validate Botpress output against schema and policy rules.
Keep Botpress limited to drafting, not execution.
Log and diff all generated transformations.
requires-engineering: add automated semantic checks before dbt execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source customer-support software with no residency or retention controls shown, while dbt-core processes data warehouse data and can reach regulated datasets. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, but the combination creates a likely compliance gap around retention and subject-rights handling unless separately configured.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes EU PII or PHI and Botpress stores related support content, compliance obligations expand.
IF retention policies differ between support logs and warehouse artifacts, mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Set explicit retention limits for support transcripts.
Keep regulated data out of Botpress workflows.
Review residency and DPA coverage for warehouse access.
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows across both systems.
